Note::TexAccessor::strip_labels¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_labels() const

Remove Anchor Declarations¶

strip_labels() removes complete \label{key} calls, including starred spelling, while retaining the prose and TeX structures around them. Labels declare cross-reference anchors but normally contribute no visible text, so their key is discarded with the call. Use labels() when those keys are data to extract, and strip_refs() for the commands that point to anchors.

The required key group is brace balanced. Nested braces therefore do not end a call early. Matching uses an exact control-word boundary: \labelled is not a label. Escaped and incomplete calls remain unchanged rather than losing a prefix or a partial key.

After deletion, ASCII whitespace is collapsed and each cell is trimmed. The method allocates a new Text Note, leaves its receiver unchanged, preserves rank and shape, and is idempotent. Undefined state propagates; defined non-Text dtypes reject. Work is linear in source bytes.

Example 1: Nested Keys, Stars, And Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \label{sec:{nested}} B \label*{starred} C)",
    R"(\\label{escaped} \labelled{long} \label{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_labels() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["A B C", "\\\\label{escaped} \\labelled{long} \\label{unfinished"]

Example 2: Matrix Position And Allocation¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(x \label{a} y)", R"(\label{b})", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_labels();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "receiver unchanged=" << (grid.at(0).find("label") != std::string_view::npos)
          << " idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_labels()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["x y", ""], 
  ["plain", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
receiver unchanged=true idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_labels().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_labels();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip labels Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip labels Int64: rejected
